references.text: The prophecy that God will pour out His Spirit on all flesh, which is the direct fulfillment of Jesus' words that the Spirit had not yet been given before His glorification.
Jesus' promise to ask the Father to give the disciples another Helper, the Spirit of truth, who will dwell in them, something that presupposes that Jesus has been glorified.
Jesus' explanation to the disciples that it is for their benefit that He goes away, for then He will send the Spirit, which happens after He has been glorified.
The historical fulfillment where Jesus, having been glorified (resurrected), breathes on the disciples and gives them the Holy Spirit.
Peter's proclamation that Jesus, who has been exalted to God's right hand (glorified), has poured out the Holy Spirit which the disciples now see and hear.
